name: Champion Iron Limited
executive_summary: Champion Iron Limited (CIA.AX) is a Quebec-based producer of high-grade iron ore concentrate, centred on the Bloom Lake mine, with a strategic pivot toward direct-reduction pellet feed (DRPF) and the acquisition of Norway's Rana Gruber. The quantitative screen rates the name a buy: nine of 22 models pass across cheapness, dividend, GARP, and risk families (composite 61%, P/E 12.0, P/B 1.4, yield 3.2%, current ratio 2.60). The valuation hook is a profitable, dividend-paying iron ore operator trading below typical cyclical-peak multiples while investing in higher-margin, decarbonisation-linked products. The central debate is whether heavy growth capex, rising leverage, a dividend reset, and M&A execution will compound earnings above the FY2024 peak, or whether commodity cyclicality and integration risk will cap returns despite attractive headline multiples. Primary filing bodies are unavailable in the source library (five ASX announcements indexed, zero downloadable extracts), limiting verification of management guidance, contingencies, and covenant language.
investment_thesis:
For a value investor, CIA.AX offers a combination of Graham-style defensibility and a visible growth option. The screen passes Graham Defensive, Graham Enterprising, Earnings Yield, Neff PEGY, Dividend Growth, Magic Formula, Acquirer's Multiple, Dreman Contrarian, and Financial Health — covering cheapness, income, growth-at-a-reasonable-price, and risk in a single name. At P/E 12.0, P/B 1.36, ROE 11.4%, and a current ratio of 2.60, the balance sheet appears conservatively structured relative to peers, even as net debt has risen with the investment cycle.

Business quality rests on Bloom Lake's position as a low-cost, high-grade concentrate producer in Quebec, with management pursuing an upmarket strategy: DRPF commissioning targets mid-2026, positioning the company to supply green-steel value chains rather than compete solely on bulk commodity pricing. News flow confirms record production milestones (Q3 FY2026), sustained dividend payments (six-month dividend declared for the period ended 31 March 2026, payable 8 July 2026), and fresh sell-side initiation (National Bank of Canada, June 2026). Recent commentary also flags a capital-priority reset and lower dividend framework (May–July 2026), which may improve balance-sheet flexibility but weakens the income pillar of the screen case.

The screen's negative trailing FCF metric (approximately –C$19.4M) warrants attention but is partly explained by a heavy capex cycle: Yahoo annual data shows FY2026 operating cash flow of C$436M against capex of C$414M, yielding modest positive FCF of C$22M — an inflection from FY2025's –C$302M FCF. The value case holds if iron ore prices remain supportive and DRPF/Rana Gruber investments earn returns above the cost of incremental debt (total debt rose to C$1.08B in FY2026 from C$800M in FY2025). Screen conviction is building (46%, four weeks at signal, stable trend), supporting an accumulate stance rather than high-conviction buy.
financial_review:
Source limitation: `filings_index.json` records regime `asx_announcements` with five indexed items — one annual (Annual Information Form for the year ended 31 March 2025, published 29 May 2025) and one interim (FY2025 fourth-quarter results, published 29 May 2025) — but zero body extracts under `filings/bodies/` (`with_body: 0`). FY2026 Q4 results (reported May 2026 per news) are not indexed. All figures below are sourced from `financials_annual.json` (Yahoo Finance); this is an explicit fallback. Interim filing language (going concern, contingencies, covenant detail) is unavailable for direct citation.

Income statement trend (Yahoo annual, CAD)

Revenue has grown steadily from C$1,395M (FY2023) to C$1,770M (FY2026), +27% over four years. Earnings are cyclical: FY2024 marked a peak (net income C$234M, basic EPS C$0.45), FY2025 saw sharp compression (net income –39% to C$142M, EPS C$0.27), and FY2026 shows partial recovery (net income C$169M, EPS C$0.32) without regaining the FY2024 high. Operating income followed a similar pattern: C$370M (FY2023) → C$428M (FY2024) → C$319M (FY2025) → C$309M (FY2026). EBITDA recovered to C$508M in FY2026 from C$446M in FY2025 but remains below the FY2024 peak of C$555M. FY2026 net income benefited from a C$16.7M gain on sale of securities (unusual item); FY2025 included a C$17.5M loss on securities.

Cached quarterly income (Yahoo) shows the most recent FY2026 quarter at revenue C$415M and net income C$23M — a materially weaker run-rate than Q3 FY2026 figures cited in news coverage (Q3 sales C$472M per earnings summaries, 29 January 2026), consistent with Q4 operational headwinds (winter weather, train derailment, planned shutdowns) reported in earnings-call summaries.

Balance sheet (Yahoo annual, FY2026)

Total assets C$3,497M; shareholders' equity C$1,534M; tangible book C$1,530M. Cash C$297M; total debt C$1,081M; net debt C$666M. Current assets C$828M / current liabilities C$319M → current ratio ~2.60 (consistent with screen). Construction in progress C$561M (DRPF and expansion capex). Net PPE C$2,420M; long-term provisions C$132M. Long-term debt C$922M (up from C$667M in FY2025 and C$508M in FY2024).

Leverage has risen meaningfully through the investment cycle. Net debt increased from C$121M (FY2023) to C$108M (FY2024) to C$549M (FY2025) to C$666M (FY2026), funded partly by C$766M long-term debt issuance in FY2026 (Yahoo cash flow). Equity grew modestly (C$1,265M → C$1,534M over three years), indicating growth is debt-financed rather than dilutive. Interest expense rose to C$43M (FY2026) from C$32M (FY2025); with EBIT of C$328M, interest coverage is approximately 7.7× — adequate but tightening versus FY2024 (EBIT C$432M, interest C$39M, coverage ~11×).

Cash flow and dividends (Yahoo annual)

Operating cash flow: C$236M (FY2023) → C$475M (FY2024) → C$304M (FY2025) → C$436M (FY2026). Capital expenditure: –C$295M → –C$343M → –C$606M → –C$414M. Free cash flow: –C$59M → C$131M → –C$302M → C$22M. Dividends paid: C$103–107M annually through the cycle.

Operating cash generation remains robust, but capex intensity peaked in FY2025 (–C$606M) before moderating. Dividends of ~C$103–107M annually have been maintained through the downturn, supporting the 3.2% screen yield but consuming most of FY2026 FCF. The screen's negative FCF figure (–C$19.4M) likely reflects a trailing-twelve-month calculation capturing the heavier capex period; annual FY2026 FCF turned marginally positive.

Interim and annual filing gap

The filing index catalogues FY2025 annual and Q4 interim announcements but provides no downloadable body text. FY2026 full-year and Q4 results (reported late May 2026 per news) are absent from the index. Covenant terms, rehabilitation provisions, tax disputes, and going-concern assessments cannot be verified from primary sources in this library.
risks_and_flags:
Commodity cyclicality. Revenue and earnings peaked in FY2024 and remain sensitive to iron ore pricing and steel demand. FY2025's earnings decline (–39% net income) demonstrates operating leverage to the commodity cycle despite volume growth. Macro context (AUD/USD 0.70, ASX 200 ~8,772 as of 24 July 2026) offers no offset — iron ore exposure dominates.

Rising leverage and capex execution. Net debt has increased sixfold from FY2024 to FY2026. FY2026 debt issuance of C$766M funds DRPF and strategic investments; failure to ramp DRPF on schedule (mid-2026 target per news) or cost overruns on C$561M construction-in-progress would pressure coverage ratios. No covenant language is available from filing bodies.

M&A integration (Rana Gruber). News reports 90% acceptance for the Rana Gruber takeover (12 March 2026), diversifying geography and product mix but adding integration, currency, and cross-border regulatory risk. Financing structure and synergy assumptions are not verifiable from primary filings in this library.

Operational disruptions. Q4 FY2026 earnings-call coverage cites winter weather, a third-party train derailment, planned shutdowns, and higher fuel costs as headwinds — a reminder of logistics and climate exposure in northern Quebec.

Dividend reset and capital-priority shift. Multiple articles (May–July 2026) reference a lower dividend and recalibrated capital framework, including *Champion Iron Shares Lag ASX Today: Dividend Cut In Framework Shift* (29 May 2026) and *Is Champion Iron (ASX:CIA) Rebalancing Capital Priorities After a Lower Dividend?* (17 July 2026). This may support balance-sheet health but directly challenges the screen's dividend-family pass.

Earnings quality and volatility. FY2026 net income includes C$16.7M in securities gains; FY2025 included a C$17.5M loss on securities. Underlying earnings power is lower and more variable than headline figures suggest. The most recent quarterly net income (C$23M) is well below the record Q3.

Governance and management transition. Two senior appointments were announced on 16 July 2026: Michael Marcotte as CFO and Steve Boucratie as Chief Legal & Strategy Officer and Corporate Secretary. Leadership changes during a capex and M&A cycle warrant monitoring; no adverse context is indicated in available sources.

Screen–fundamentals tension. The screen passes Financial Health and dividend models, yet trailing FCF is negative and leverage is rising. Pension/post-retirement benefit provisions (C$13M current, C$132M long-term provisions per Yahoo balance sheet) are present but cannot be assessed against filing disclosures.

Source coverage gap. Without downloadable ASX annual reports or interim announcement bodies in the library, material risks (environmental liabilities, indigenous consultation, mine-life assumptions, related-party transactions) cannot be evaluated from primary regulatory text.
news_highlights:
Coverage over the past year is moderate (30 articles in manifest) and skewed toward earnings summaries, dividend commentary, and sell-side opinion rather than investigative reporting.

Strategy and operations
- *Champion Iron Record Quarter Highlights DRPF Progress And Rana Gruber Offer* (29 January 2026): Record quarterly sales and production at Bloom Lake; DRPF initial commissioning underway; first DRPF shipments targeted mid-2026; cash tender offer for Rana Gruber launched.
- *Champion Iron (ASX:CIA) Posts Record 3.9M Tonne Quarter as Green Steel Plant Enters Commissioning* (2 February 2026): Record production quarter; DRPF commissioning milestone.
- *Champion Iron secures 90% acceptance for Rana Gruber takeover* (12 March 2026): M&A progressing toward completion.
- *Champion Iron Reports Q4 FY2026 Results as DRPF Project Nears Completion* (28 May 2026) and *Champion Iron Q4 Earnings Call Highlights* (28 May 2026): Higher YoY Q4 production but weather, train derailment, shutdowns, and fuel costs weighed on logistics and costs.
- *Champion Iron announces production gains and new growth projects* (30 April 2026): Ongoing expansion narrative.

Capital markets and sentiment
- *National Bank of Canada Initiates Coverage of Champion Iron, Oceanic Iron Ore* (10 June 2026) and *National Bank Coverage Puts Spotlight On Champion Iron Valuation Gap* (11 June 2026): New Canadian sell-side coverage.
- *Bullish: Analysts Just Made A Huge Upgrade To Their Champion Iron Limited (ASX:CIA) Forecasts* (21 April 2026): Consensus earnings upgrades.
- *Vanguard Group Becomes Substantial Holder in Champion Iron Limited* (13 July 2026): Institutional accumulation signal.
- *Champion Iron Shares Fall to Six-Year Low: Here's What Is Weighing on CIA* (24 June 2026): Share-price weakness despite operational progress.

Corporate actions and governance
- *Champion Iron Shares Lag ASX Today: Dividend Cut In Framework Shift* (29 May 2026): Dividend reduction tied to capital-allocation reset — material for income investors.
- *Champion Iron Limited Announces Actual Ordinary Fully Paid Dividend for the Six Months Ended March 31, 2026, Payable on July 8, 2026* (2 July 2026): Dividend continuity at reduced level.
- *Champion Iron Limited Announces Appointment of Michael Marcotte as Chief Financial Officer* (16 July 2026) and *…Steve Boucratie as Chief Legal & Strategy Officer and Corporate Secretary* (16 July 2026): Senior leadership changes.
- *Champion Iron Limited Announces Cessation of Certain Securities* (7 July 2026): Likely routine securities housekeeping.

News coverage is adequate for tracking strategic direction but thin on regulatory, environmental, or governance controversy. No material adverse regulatory actions appear in the manifest.
research_rationale: Deep research largely confirms the screen's value case on multiples and balance-sheet liquidity, but the absence of primary filing bodies, rising leverage, dividend reset, and unproven DRPF/M&A execution prevent full confirmation of the buy signal.
